newsitem.title: FRANCE: FOCUS-Bank of France trims key interest rate.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Bank of France trims key interest rate.

text.p: The Bank of France said on Thursday it was shaving five points off the key official intervention rate in what economists read as yet another highly cautious step which left room for further monetary easing.

The central bank said after a meeting of its monetary policy council that it was cutting the intervention rate by five basis points to 3.20 percent from 3.25 percent, the tenth of a string of small cuts this year.

Fifteen of 20 economists polled by Reuters on Tuesday had said the relatively healthy performance of the French franc in recent times had provided a "window of opportunity" for a cut and some said news of record unemployment on Thursday morning would only serve to reinforce the issue.
"It was expected. It leaves a margin of manoeuvre for later. They can do the same thing next month to narrow against the German repo (rate)," said Nathalie Fillet, bond analyst at Paribas bank.

"There is no domestic or international reason for the Bank to stop cutting interest rates. It is moving with caution, but I think that in five basis point steps, it can bring the intervention rate to parity with the German repo rate," said Valerie Asselot, economist at Credit Lyonnais. The German repo rate now stands at 3.00 percent.

"It is in many ways a symbolic cut because it's true the macroeconomic impact of such a small rate cut is not going to be major," she said. "Basically the Bank of France is signalling that they are doing what they can do."
The Bank continued to post its less important five-to-10 day rate at 4.75 percent.

The intervention rate, at which the Bank of France allocates repo funds, was last cut, on September 19, 1996 from 3.35 percent. On August 1 the Bank cut 15 basis points off its five-to-10 day rate from 4.90 percent.
